newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK local govt members to stay on after handover.
newsitem.headline: HK local govt members to stay on after handover.

text.p: Members of Hong Kong's civic councils and advisory district boards will stay on after the territory reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, future leader Tung Chee-hwa said.

The 41 members of the Urban Council, the 39 members of the Regional Council and members of the 18 District Boards will continue to serve after the handover, Tung's office said in a statement issued late on Monday.

The two councils, overseeing matters including environmental hygiene and recreation, sports and cultural facilities, will each be expanded to a membership of 50 after the transfer of rule, the statement said.
The District Boards, which advise the government on district administration, will also be enlarged, it said.

All of the 41 existing Urban Council members were elected. Of the 39 existing Regional Council members, 36 were elected and three are ex-officio members, the chairman and two vice-chairmen of the Heung Yee Kuk, a rural-based organisation of male village elders. All existing members of the District Boards are elected. Tung has already appointed the additional members to Urban Council, Regional Council and District Boards.
Britain hands Hong Kong back to China on July 1, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
